newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 3.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 3.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Another strand in News' global pay television strategy appears to fraying, with a report in The Sydney Morning Herald on Tuesday that Telstra is in talks with News Ltd to shorten the cable rollout for their Foxtel cable television joint venture from four million homes to its current two million homes.

Speculation about Foster's launching a share buy-back and placement of the 51 percent of stakes owned by BHP and Asahi continues, with The Australian saying on Tuesday the deals could be announced as early as Wednesday.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$19.15 (+0.292)

Chevron's chairman and CEO Ken Durr told the Australian Financial Review the WAPET consortium is on the verge of recommending a plan to effectively merge production from WAPET's Gorgon field with production from the North West Shelf (NWS) consortium (which includes BHP and Woodside), increasing the size of production at NWS's Karratha LNG facility. It would also increase Australian LNG supply and competition for Japanese LNG demand.
Australian biotechnology group ForBio Ltd FBO.AX said on

Monday it intended to seek a secondary listing either on the London Stock Exchange or the pan-European Easdaq market, to raise funds for expansion. ForBio said it had met institutions to complete a private placing to raise around $5.0 million but would be seeking around $20 to $25 million when it floats in Europe.

Sporting goods retailer Rebel Sport said on Monday its 26 percent full-year net profit rise had been achieved despite tough conditions for the sector. The company reported a net profit of A$3.91 million for the year ended March 31 compared to A$3.09 million the previous year.
